notes.linkC: A final consonant moves over to the next syllable when that syllable begins with a silent consonant letter, so it sounds linked.
notes.doubleC: Of two final consonants, only one is pronounced before a consonant, but before a vowel the second one links to the next syllable.
notes.neutral: At the end of a word or before a consonant, a final consonant is pronounced as only one of a few basic sounds.
notes.hDrop: The h sound is silent after a vowel or n, m, l, ng; the neighbouring sounds then link smoothly.
notes.nasal: A p, t or k sound becomes m, n or ng when a nasal consonant follows.
notes.lateral: The sound n next to l is pronounced l.
notes.rToN: An l sound after a stop or ng is pronounced n, and a stop before it may also turn nasal.
notes.wolLink: A final l sound links to the next vowel-initial syllable, so the syllable boundary does not match the spelling.
